alerts.title: Pregnancy viral load monitoring due at 3 months and at 28 weeks
alerts.message: Guidelines state that for pregnant women on ART, viral load should be checked at baseline and after 3 months of ART, with a repeat at delivery if gestation is over 28 weeks. Routine monitoring for pregnant and lactating women is every 3 months. The patient is 22 weeks pregnant, 10 weeks into ART, with viral load 89 copies/mL (suppressed) from 125,000 at diagnosis, so the 3-month check is due now and a further check is needed at or after 28 weeks. The clinician's plan is blank, so no monitoring order is documented.

evidence.recommended_action: Document a plan for the 3-month viral load in pregnancy and schedule a repeat viral load at or after 28 weeks' gestation or at delivery per the pregnancy monitoring table.

alerts.title: Dolutegravir and iron supplement co-administration needs timing review
alerts.message: Guidelines advise caution with DTG and divalent cation-containing medications in pregnancy, since pregnant women frequently receive iron supplements. The patient takes ferrous sulfate alongside TLD, and her Hb is 10.8 g/dL, so iron therapy is likely to continue. No administration timing is documented in the plan. Interaction severity is limited, but the absorption interaction is relevant to ongoing anaemia management.

evidence.recommended_action: Review timing of ferrous sulfate relative to dolutegravir per the guideline and document separation instructions in the plan.

alerts.title: Confirm DTG-based regimen continuation in pregnancy
alerts.message: Guidelines state that women who become pregnant while on DTG-based regimens should be maintained on the regimen. The patient is on TDF/3TC/DTG and is 22 weeks pregnant, so the current regimen is appropriate. No regimen change is indicated, but the plan should explicitly document continuation.

evidence.recommended_action: Document in the plan that TDF/3TC/DTG is continued through pregnancy and transition to TLD postpartum per guidelines.

screening_bundle.quote: TABLE 21: Timing of viral load monitoring during pregnancy, delivery and breastfeeding. Period ART initiation in pregnancy Already on ART at diagnosis of pregnancy Previously taken ART, not currently on treatment (ART interruption, ART for PMTCT) Newly diagnosed HIV infection during delivery or breastfeeding Antenatal VL at baseline and after 3 months of ART: if > 28 weeks' gestation, then repeat VL at delivery VL at first ANC visit VL at initiation of DTG-based regimen; repe

etween DTG and divalent cation-containing medication in pregnancy, since pregnant women frequently receive iron or calcium supplements and/or magnesium-/aluminium- containing antacids (see module 17). Patients returning to care in pregnancy after interrupting a first-line NNRTI regimen or those exposed to previous VTP regimens should be put directly on a DTG-based regimen, rather than retrying an NNRTI-regimen (see also module 16). As per the current PMTCT guidelines, women n

-9 months postpartum when they should be transitioned to TLD if the VL within the past 6 months is suppressed. - Women becoming pregnant while on DTG-based regimens shall be maintained on the regimen. - Treatment should be monitored by measuring viral load 6 months after initiation of ART and every 6-12 months or when clinically indicated. - A repeat viral load of >1000cells/mm3 suggests treatment failure and is indication for HIV DR and appropriate switch after ruling out ad

The ACTG A5372 trial showed that DTG needs to be given twice daily for 28 days if co-administered with rifapentine. 137 Rifapentine also affects the metabolism of common ARV drugs most affected by CYP induction such as all protease inhibitors (PIs) including LPV/r, and some non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs), including nevirapine. 138 All patients receiving ART should be considered for TPT after having been screened for active TB using a symptom screen,

ssed, then genotype testing is recommended.
